line.line: All right, then.
Cause trouble in Whiterun, and I'll haul you into the Dragonsreach dungeon myself.
Let me guess - someone stole your sweetroll...
Hey, no fair! Get her, Stump!
Until next time.
What do you want?
Need something?
Well, one of us has to do something!
Be careful!
I said no! No adventures, no theatrics, no thief-chasing!
Well, what are you going to do then, huh? Let's hear it!
We are done talking about this.
Oh, a customer. Sorry you had to hear that.
You could? I've got some coin coming in from my last shipment. It's yours if you bring my claw back.
Maybe you could talk some sense into my pig-headed brother.
Now, if you're going to get those thieves, you should head to Bleak Falls Barrow, northwest of town.
So this is your plan, Lucan?
Be careful!
Yes. So now you don't have to go, do you?
Oh really? Well I think your new helper here needs a guide.
Wh- no... I... Oh, by the Eight, fine. But only to the edge of town!
This way.
Then what are you wasting my time for?
We have to go through town and across the bridge to get to Bleak Falls Barrow.
That letter ought to convince Camilla to never speak to Faendal ever again.
Those thieves must be mad, hiding out there. Those old crypts are filled with nothing but traps, trolls, and who knows what else!
Orgnar.
Hard not to.
The ale is going bad. We need to get a new batch.
Did you hear me?
Yep. Ale's going bad.
I guess you don't have potatoes in your ears after all. Just make sure we get a fresh batch in soon.
Welcome. Let me know if you want anything... think I got a clean mug around here somewhere.
Until next time.
Welcome. Let me know if you want anything... think I got a clean mug around here somewhere.
Show those thieves not to steal from Lucan Valerius!
The sooner you find the claw, the sooner our lives can get back to normal.
Until next time.
This is an ode to Skyrim's staunch protectors... the Imperials.
We drink to our youth, to days come and gone. For the age of aggression is just about done.
We'll drive out the Stormcloaks and restore what we own. With our blood and our steel we'll take back our home.
Down with Ulfric the killer of kings. On the day of your death we'll drink and we'll sing.
We're the children of Skyrim, and we fight all our lives. And when Sovngarde beckons, every one of us dies!
But this land is ours and we'll see it wiped clean. Of the scourge that has sullied our hopes and our dreams.
An epic, to be precise.  One that's coming to its climax.  There's a tower on the horizon, canvassed by a sky the color of blood.
As I ride my steed closer, I see that coiled around the tower like a serpent is the evil dragon Numinex resurrected by Alduin.
He roars at the sight of me, and I answer him by raising the Sword of Dawn, shining like a beacon through the darkness.
I ride fast and low, evading the sweep of his talons.  I enter the tower where my princess awaits, but my task is not yet complete.
A direct attack is foolish.  Numinex knows this. That's why I do it.  My aim is to shock him just long enough to run up his nose and behind his eyes.
Where the tender spot in his neck awaits my blade.
You're that visitor, been pokin' around.
What are you doing that for?
Come on in. Just stoked the fire. Take a seat and get the cold out.
You're new around here, so I'll go easy on ya. But don't get on my bad side.
Ain't used to strangers here in Riverwood.
All right, then.
That's a decent weapon you've made there.
Iron or steel is what you need. Leave that fancy Elven stuff to the Elves.
Hmm hmm.
Nobody believes me, but I tell you, I saw a dragon!
By Shor, what do you want?
Safe travels.
And what might you need? Hmm?
Gods! Another fight.
Do you think Tiber Septim ever fought here? You know... Here! Wow...
These are dark days... at least we know we're making our part to make things better, eh?
Citizen, I'm warning you. Your presence is interfering with Imperial business. Be gone!
If you know any true sons and daughters of Skyrim, tell them to head to Windhelm. Ulfric Stormcloak wants to see them.
(meow)
Mercy!
Don't take this the wrong way, but you look a little sickly.
M'aiq wishes you well.
Need something?
By Ysmir, it's true. A jester - funny suit and all. Just north, by the Loreius Farm. Fool had a coffin in a cart, with a broken wheel.
Like to see him laugh his way out of that.
Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!
Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!
Good. Chat time's over.
Ride strong.
Need a horse? Talk to my father, Skulvar.
Well, sounds like you've had quite the journey, Uthgerd. But you were gone longer than usual. I got to thinking maybe you weren't coming back...
Yeah?
All right, then.
Be careful!
Yes?
What do you need?
No lollygaggin'.
We'll pay whatever it takes, but we must have more swords for the Imperial soldiers.
I just can't fill an order that size on my own.
Ha! I'd sooner bend my knee to Ulfric Stormcloak.
Have it your way. I'll take the job, but don't expect a miracle.
Don't forget to check inside the shop if you need anything.
They say Helgen got hit by a dragon. One of those horrors comes here, we'll be ready.
Trouble?
Remember, fresh fruit and vegetables every day. Mostly.
Thank you, thank you. No, please, hold your applause.
Come on in. Just stoked the fire. Take a seat and get the cold out.
One more song, what say you? Yeah? All right, then!
Nnnnooowwwwwww...
Good afternoon.
There once was a hero named Ragnar the Red, who came riding to Whiterun from ole Rorikstead!
It's the leaving that's hardest, I know.
One of these days, I'll really have to get something that's more comfortable to wear. And easier to put on. *sighs*
Now please, no more questions.
Want to hear a little Nord wisdom? You don't really know a woman 'til you've had a strong drink and a fistfight with her.
I don't have to take that from you!
Come on! Come on!
Come on. Let's see what you're made of.
A fight!
Get her!
Get her!
Enough... of this!
Oof!
It's... nothing...
Drive that snowback to the ground. Come on!
Not bad! Keep your guard up and wait for an opening!
Nargh!
Keep it together! Don't let them gain further ground!
Come on! Come on!
Ugh! That it? That your best?
I can take you!
Oof!
Weergh!
Get her!
Just keep your guard up!
Argh!
Who taught you to fight? Keep those hands up!
Weergh!
Fight! Fight!
Don't let her get away with this!
Nargh!
This should be good.
This is the end for you!
Fight! Fight!
Weergh!
Yeah! Come on!
You win. On my honor, Carlotta won't have to worry about me ever again.
Foolish old woman! You know nothing! Nothing of our struggles, our suffering!
The finest cuts, fresh from the wilds!
Nothing? And what of my son? Hmm? What of Thorald? Is he nothing? So don't talk to me about suffering!
Your son chose his side, and he chose poorly. And now he's gone. Such is the way of war. The sooner you accept his loss, the better.
Tired of bread and stew? Had enough of fish and fowl? Treat yourself and your kin to a choice cut of steak or a tender rack of ribs!
I will never accept his death! My son still lives. I feel it in my heart. So tell me, Battle-Borns, where is he? Where are you holding my Thorald?
Do you believe this old hag?
"Holding him?" Why I've got him in my cellar. He's my prisoner.
Chops and steaks fit for a Jarl! Come and see my selection of the finest-quality meats!
"I breathe now, in royalty, and reshape this land which is mine. I do this for you, Red Legions, for I love you."
Aye, love. Love! Even as man, great Talos cherished us. For he saw in us, in each of us, the future of Skyrim! The future of Tamriel!
Until next time.
Always good to see 'em go.
I'm surprised you had the wits to notice, Olfrid, what with your nose buried so far up the Emperor's backside.
And there it is, friends! The ugly truth! We are the children of man! Talos is the true god of man! Ascended from flesh, to rule the realm of spirit!
You won't be laughing when the Thalmor come to root out Stormcloak sympathizers.
The very idea is inconceivable to our Elven overlords! Sharing the heavens with us? With man? Ha! They can barely tolerate our presence on earth!
I'll remember that when the Stormcloaks liberate the city. No amount of money will protect you then, Battle-Born.
Ain't nobody high and mighty in these halls, exceptin' the Jarl. And don't you forget!
There is a thing you could do for me. Suitable for someone of your particular talents, perhaps.
Farengar, I think I've found someone who can help you with your dragon project.
Go ahead and fill her in with all the details.
I've got my eyes on you.
This is a priority now. Anything we can use to fight this dragon, or dragons. We need it, quickly. Before it's too late.
Of course, Jarl Balgruuf. You seem to have found me an able assistant.
I'm sure she will prove most useful.
Bring back this tablet that Farengar wants and I'll be in your debt.
Succeed at this, and you'll be rewarded. Whiterun will be in your debt.
And what does the Empire do? Nothing! Nay, worse than nothing! The Imperial machine enforces the will of the Thalmor! Against its own people!
Until next time.

Huh?
Huh?
Hey, a fight!
I knew it!
Are those two at it again?
A fight!
Come on now, watch the footwork. Keep your balance.
Nice!
All right!
Just keep swinging!
Agh!
This should be good.
Argh, filthy n'wah!
Nargh!
If death is what you seek, you'll get your wish!
Going to enjoy killing you!
Azura curse you!
Get 'em! Kill 'em!
All right, then.
No more! I yield! I yield!
Hmm hmm.
I'd be dead if not for Vignar. He took me in and helped me turn my life around.
Oh, I'm just a servant, dear. You want to talk to one of the Companions, I'm sure.
My brother Vilkas is a better talker than me. He should be around someplace.
All right, then.
Hmm hmm.
Goodbye, dear.
I had a bad time a few years back, an' I turned to drink. But Vignar, he wouldn't let me stay weak.
And there it is, friends! The ugly truth! We are the children of man! Talos is the true god of man! Ascended from flesh, to rule the realm of spirit!
I know your family's honor is important to you, but we can't afford it!
It took me weeks to find that thieves' den. I can't stop now, and I can't get the sword on my own.
Battle-Born! Give me your money!
So you're willing to starve your wife and daughter to reclaim some rusty old sword?
I... I don't have any money.
I just need to hire one, maybe two good men. You won't starve.
You better give me five septims right now, or I'm gonna bloody your nose...
Please, let's speak privately.
I'll put it plainly. You can claim your sword, or you can keep your wife. If you set foot outside that gate, I won't be here when you return.
No! Please! I really don't have any money, Braith! I'll give you ten septims tomorrow. Just don't hit me.
I just want to go home and read.
Saffir!
Ten septims tomorrow, baby Battle-Born. Or I'm gonna bloody your nose and your lip.
If you find that sword, please bring it to me.
Wait... I...
Money, you laggard! What else? It always comes down to coin.
Welcome to our home.
Mother, what's the meaning of this? Who have you brought into our home?
Avulstein, put that down! She's here to help us find Thorald!
How do we know she's not spying for the Battle-Born? This was foolish!
We can't trust anyone! Who knows what they'll do if they find me here.
I can't take any more of this. No weapons, please. Let's just talk.
All right, Mother.
You lost?
Best if... you didn't mention to anyone that you saw me here.
You take care of yourself, now.
I fear the night. Because the werewolves and vampires don't.
A fine day to you, friend. May you die with a sword in your hands.
Welcome. Let me know if you want anything... think I got a clean mug around here somewhere.
Now please, no more questions.
If he comes back here, I'll have to talk with Balgruuf and get that fool cast out for good...
All the gold in Hammerfell isn't worth cleaning up another pool of vomit...
You're very welcome. Enjoy your time here in Whiterun and let me know if you need another drink!
We drink to our youth, to days come and gone. For the age of aggression is just about done.
We'll drive out the Stormcloaks and restore what we own. With our blood and our steel we'll take back our home.

This is a local favorite and one of the first songs I ever learned. Ragnar the Red.
Welcome, traveller... it's always nice to see a friendly face at the Mare!
Oh! There once was a hero named Ragnar the Red, who came riding to Whiterun from ole Rorikstead!
And the braggart did swagger and brandish his blade, as he told of bold battles and gold he had made!
But then he went quiet, did Ragnar the Red, when he met the shieldmaiden Matilda who said...
"Oh, you talk and you lie and you drink all our mead! Now I think it's high time that you lie down and bleed!"
And so then came the clashing and slashing of steel, as the brave lass Matilda charged in full of zeal!
And the braggart named Ragnar was boastful no moooooree... when his ugly red head rolled around on the floor!
Need anything else, just let me know.
I'll show you to your room. Right this way.
You're the best! Can you be my mother?
